## Steps

<figure class="story-hero"><a href="/forge-studio/media/stories/S3/01-open-studio-on-the-projects-pillar.png"><img src="/forge-studio/media/stories/S3/01-open-studio-on-the-projects-pillar.png" alt="1. Open Studio on the Projects pillar"></a></figure>

1. **Open Studio on the Projects pillar.** The Projects pillar lists every project forge manages.
2. **Open the project.** The project page is where the contract lives: what forge tests with, what it demos with, what it releases with, and which skills its agents may reach for.
3. **Count the skills this project binds.** Nine skills — an API explorer, a resource scaffolder, a docs generator, an acceptance-test author.
4. **Read the first of them.** It does not resolve.
5. **Press "Rebuild contract", and read the drift report it produces before applying it.** One press, and the report is already real — this ground needs no template named at all.
6. **Apply the rebuild.** Rebuilding is not repairing.
7. **Check the nine skills resolve now.** The rebuild moved the skills to where the current contract expects them and rewrote the wiring that points at them.
8. **Check the secrets the rebuild had no right to touch.** This is the first of the three things a rebuild must never regenerate.
9. **Check the instructions still point at the project’s own file.** The second.
10. **Check the north star survived.** The third.
11. **Confirm preflight is MET and the project is still ready for a Flow.** This is the check that says the reset was worth doing rather than merely survivable.
12. **Run the onboarding agent to re-derive the parts a template cannot write, briefed with the contract’s own north star and gate.** A template can regenerate the mechanisms forge owns.
13. **Follow "View onboarding session" and watch it work.** The session opens on the shared session surface, showing the same five-element contract buildout the project page shows — so the operator watches the Agent finish the job in the vocabulary the gate will judge.
